More Texans support me than believe I can win.
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
Peter,
In just a minute, I’m going to personally ask you to **[make a $5 donation to my campaign for governor.](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20261028_1_cavalry.EyQSfe&refcode=em20261028-2564&amount=5&t=1&akid=2564%2E299639%2E-EqXHi)**
Before I do, there's something I need supporters outside of Texas to understand.
A recent Marist poll has me ahead of Greg Abbott, 49% to 46%. _But only 28% of Texans think I'll actually win_.
I think I know why. **Texans have learned to expect that we'll be left to fight Abbott's machine alone, and as long as they believe that, they won't believe we can win.**
_You can change that_. Every donation from outside Texas tells voters here that they're not on their own this time, and that this race is winnable, because it is.

subject: Know Before You Vote: [Or What You Don’t Know Before you Vote]
body:
| | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/philscott/know-before-you-vote-or-what-you-dont-know-before-you-vote?e=19cebfe173)

#

# **Know Before You Vote: [Or What You Don’t Know Before You Vote] **
_**The questions no one is asking: how do you pay for it?**_ The primary theme of Amanda Janoo’s policy proposals is simple: tax and spend. And the fact is,**that’s not change.** That’s the same old approach of the legislative majority and the one-party rule that existed before Governor Scott came to office. What’s new is that, one week before the election, Vermonters have not been told how the math works by the candidate or the media. And to be clear, it doesn’t work. Vermonters deserve to know, when the math does not add up. How does Janoo plan to pay for everything she has promised? _Universal Primary Care:_ Conservative estimates for universal primary care come in around $600 million. Janoo’s “Fair Share” tax (on households of $250,000 or more) raises about $300 million. That is a $300 million gap in her budget - for just one policy. Not to mention, Janoo’s fellow “Fair Share” coalition advocates have other plans for the money to [“insulate the state from federal funding cuts.”](https://us.list-manage.com/vpULq1XhQwZ?e=19cebfe173&c2id=84d1094b3a168b6495ef78aca9f3540c) Janoo should be asked:**How do you intend to pay for this campaign promise, especially when members of your own party do not agree on the financing? ** _Vermont Public Bank_ : When this idea was considered in the past, Democratic Treasurer Beth Pearce said it would put our bond rating at risk - risk that gets paid by taxpayers. And, it will cost $50 million to 100 million to capitalize. Janoo should be asked**: How will this work or how will she pay for it? ** _Property Taxes:_**** Amanda Janoo said she wants to raise $1 billion in property taxes on second homes. That’s about a**$30,000 average increase per unit.** Janoo should be asked:**What are the economic consequences of this idea? Or how does it prevent future tax increases to pay for education?** _Federal Funding_ : Janoo continues to argue Vermont should be “reducing our reliance” on federal funding. Vermonters contribute about $6.45 billion in federal taxes. And we get back about $3.2 billion in federal funds, which is about one-third of the state’s $9.19 billion budget. And, importantly, federal funding represents taxes Vermonters are already paying and will have to continue to pay whether we accept federal funds or not. Janoo should be asked: **By how much will you reduce our reliance on federal funds, and how will you close the resulting budget gap? ** _The Economy:_ Janoo has conveyed well-documented opposition to economic growth as a priority. And has said, her purpose in life... “[is] to transform the global economic system,” using Vermont as an incubator along the way. The basic math problem: An economy that is not growing is an economy in recession. During the last real recession, the state had to cut services and raise taxes to balance the budget. Janoo should be asked: **How can you deliver on your promise of more government spending while deliberately shrinking the economy?** Every candidate’s policy platform deserves a critical analysis. Vermonters deserve answers, so we’ll continue to ask the questions no one else is:**How do you pay for your promises? And are they good for Vermont? **

_-Team Scott_

Peter, If you’ve been keeping an eye on the fight to retake a Democratic majority in the Senate, you probably already know that competitive seats in states like Maine, Texas, and Alaska are currently in play for Democrats. That is massively exciting news. But as much as I want Democrats to win those races, we have to be realistic about the math. The fact of the matter is that **Republicans only need to flip Michigan in order to hold onto their majority.** If they flip this seat in Michigan, our chances at winning the Senate are _toast_. I don’t say all this to scare you, but I want to be honest about what this means for our race:
* Republicans have made me their **#1 target to beat** in November, and they are dropping $1 million a day on ads from now until Election Day.

* That means the hundreds of thousands of Michiganders who are currently choosing whether to vote for me, Mike Rogers, or whether to even vote at all are being **swamped with attack ads** in this final push.

We have already defied the odds once and fought this race to a virtual tie. Now, we have to finish the job. The window to make a difference in the outcome of this race is closing fast, so if you’ve been waiting for the right moment to make a contribution to our campaign, _this is it_. [Will you please donate $10 to my campaign and the Democratic Party of Georgia so we can hold onto this must-win Senate seat? To all of Cait Conley’s supporters: Please don’t click away from this important email. This isn’t the first time we’ve reached out, so we’ll get straight to the point. We’re emailing to ask you to make a donation to help Cait Conley beat Mike Lawler. If everyone reading this donated literally $1, we would not only be able to fight back against Mike Lawler and his MAGA billionaire donors, we’d also have the resources to fund our on-the-ground voter outreach efforts. Unlike Mike, Cait doesn’t depend on a handful of billionaires to bail this campaign out. We’re powered by grassroots donations. Last quarter, over 90% of contributions to our team were less than $100. Without emails like this one, we wouldn’t have a chance. clean_body: | = Hey Peter, we wanted to make sure you saw the message our executive director Michelle White sent last week. Election Day is in just six days, and it’s clear that momentum is with EMILYs List women running to take back power at every level of government. But this is not the time to get complacent. Our women are still counting on a final surge of support so that they have what they need to turn out every last voter. = | = Thank you. — the EMILYs List team \-------------Original Message------------- Sent: October 19, 2026 From: Michelle White, EMILYs List = Hi Peter, I'm Michelle White, executive director of EMILYs List. My job is to lead the staff of this organization and make sure we have the budget, resources, and strategy we need to elect Democratic pro-choice women at every level of government. I want to be very direct about why that matters. EMILYs List was founded because women candidates were not getting the early support they needed to run credible, competitive campaigns. Ellen Malcolm and a group of groundbreaking women knew that if women were going to win elections, they needed early money, real fundraising power, and a donor network that believed in them before the political establishment caught up. That's why EMILYs List exists. And from the very beginning, this work was about people willing to invest early —people who understood that money is not just money in a campaign. It is credibility. It is staff. It is voter contact. It is the difference between being written off and being taken seriously — between winning and losing. With just 15 days left until Election Day, we are all gas, no brakes. This is a time where I need to call on supporters like you to make a critical final investment in our work to make sure our women have what they need to win. = = The history of EMILYs List matters, but I am writing today because our work and mission cannot just exist in the past. The work we do matters more than ever right now. Every day, our staff is working to recruit, train, support, and elect Democratic pro-choice women who can change the direction of this country. Our team is helping candidates build stronger campaigns. We are raising the money they need to compete. We are studying races, voters, issues, and opposition. We are communicating with millions of supporters about what is at stake. We are running paid programs to help our candidates win in some of the most competitive races in the country. And behind every email, every endorsement, and every strategic decision is a team of people who are very, very good at what they do. I will say this plainly: This is the best team in politics. I see their work up close every day. I see the long hours, the strategic thinking, the creativity, the discipline, and the urgency the EMILYs List staff bring to this fight. I see people who know that electing women is not just about winning elections – it's about changing who has power in this country and what they do with it. But talent, smarts, and strategy are not enough. To do this work at the scale this moment demands, we need resources. We need to invest in our candidates. Folks,
**I have a critical update to share with you:** Recently, Nate Silver's Silver Bulletin has shifted his prediction for North Carolina's U.S. Senate race further in our direction.
A lot of folks will hear that and think it means that we can rest on our laurels for these last six days. That we can pat ourselves on the back and put up our feet, since a win is guaranteed.
Having won my fair share of tough statewide races, trust me: **That couldn 't be further from the truth.**
While it means our campaign clearly has what it takes to flip this seat, it also means that the GOP is growing increasingly desperate to defeat me. Far-right super PACs have spent millions to broadcast despicable lies about my record on the airwaves, and BOTH President Trump and JD Vance just came for another recent hurrah to rally the MAGA base in Greenville and Hendersonville.
The tides may be turning against Republicans in North Carolina and nationwide, but Senate control still hinges on the outcome of our race. **Your grassroots support toward our daily fundraising goal is the only way I 'll fight back against any surprises they still have up their sleeves and cross the finish line first on Election Day.**
[So if you care about flipping North Carolina blue and taking back the Senate as much as I do, will you chip in $5 now to power our movement to victory?](https://substack.com/redirect/eccd3531-daa4-4006-8430-6ad8dbd1a8f7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
[Donate](https://substack.com/redirect/eccd3531-daa4-4006-8430-6ad8dbd1a8f7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Thanks so much for sticking with me,
Roy Cooper

By October 23, roughly 280,000 black North Carolinians had already voted early -- about 60 percent ahead of the same point in 2022, according to VoteHub's 2026 Early Vote Tracker, built with the L2 voter file. Tennessee's early vote is up 62 percent. South Carolina passed its entire 2022 early-voting total in a little over six days -- nearly 564,000 ballots, a record. In Louisiana, black turnout is pacing at rates rarely seen since 2008, the last time a presidential-level wave pulled the state's electorate forward. Michael McDonald, the University of Florida professor who has been counting early votes since Florida made that a full-time job, reported Sunday that early turnout across six Southern states is running strongest among black and Hispanic voters. Bloomberg's summary put the mechanism in one line: black turnout surging in the South as the voting-rights fallout lands.
The fallout has a name and a date. On April 29, the Supreme Court decided 'Louisiana v. Callais', 6-3, with Justice Alito writing for the majority and Justice Kagan dissenting for the three Democratic appointees. The Court held that Louisiana's second majority-Black congressional district -- created to comply with Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act -- was an _unconstitutional racial gerrymander_. Section 2, as the majority reinterpreted it, requires a strong inference of intentional discrimination, not merely discriminatory effect: the intent standard Congress expressly rejected when it amended the Act in 1982. The NAACP Legal Defense Fund called it an evisceration of the section. Around 140 House districts nationwide are majority-minority; the decision put the logic behind many of them on notice.
Then came the number that should interest anyone who cares about voters rather than narratives. VoteHub's analysis of majority-Black Black Belt counties found their turnout edge grew from 1.1 points in the elections before the ruling to 5.9 points in the elections after it. Nothing about the mechanics of voting changed on April 29. The information did.
That is the observation, and I want to state the opinion under it plainly: **it is a good thing to have more informed voters**. Not "voters who agree with me" -- that is the definition every campaign, church bulletin, and cable hit quietly uses. I mean the inconvenient, symmetric version: citizens who know what happened and vote anyway. An informed electorate is the only constituency that cannot be owned. It votes against its informers as readily as with them, banks its own conclusions, and shows up in numbers that embarrass everyone's models. If a party finds informed voters threatening, the finding is the confession.
What happened in the Black Belt this fall is information discipline at its purest. A long opinion with footnotes about illustrative maps and Gingles preconditions became, within weeks, required reading in the places it was actually about. The chain was not mysterious: the ruling, then the county explainer, then the barbershop, then the church social hall, then the early-vote line. Nobody had to be convinced the matter was urgent; the Court had already ruled on the weight of their votes. When information arrives with your name attached, consumption is not a problem. People read what assesses them.
There is also a register of history worth naming without melodrama. This is an electorate that has been made to re-read its own eligibility more often than any other in America: the Fifteenth Amendment in 1870, the Act in 1965, Shelby County's gutting of preclearance in 2013, 'Callais' in 2026. Each time the status was reopened, the response eventually showed up in the poll books. That is not grievance; it is a discipline -- arguably the most consistently informed habit in American political life. The textbooks say voters are supposed to study the rules. Only one group of voters has had to study the rules about whether they may vote, and has done the homework every time.
Two honest caveats, because a surge is not a theorem. Turnout is not the same as being informed; mobilization can ride the same bus as education. Early votes are banked, not won -- McDonald himself cautions that the composition of the early electorate does not guarantee the composition of the final one, and North Carolina's lagging mail ballots keep the 2022 comparisons fuzzier than the headlines suggest. And being informed is not a season; it is a practice. The unphotogenic elections -- school boards, county commissions, the off-years where the next map and the next ruling get drafted -- are where this syllabus either stays open or quietly closes.
But on the main point I will take the cheerful position without apology: **a voter who read the ruling before voting is the system working** , wherever they land on the ballot. Informed voters are not a partisan asset. They are an operational hazard to everyone who preferred them confused, and the republic has no better friends than that.
My pieces usually end asking "Who decided?" -- a question about choices made over everyone's heads, in rooms with the good lighting. This time the ledger reads differently. The Court decided the syllabus. The parties decided the venues. But a 4.8-point swing in the Black Belt's turnout edge was decided nowhere but the early-vote lines themselves. For once, the answer is printed where everyone can check it, one name at a time: they did.

One week out from Election Day, the best civics classroom in America is a parking lot with a voting machine in it. | | | Oct 28 | | | | | | | | | | | | By October 23, roughly 280,000 black North Carolinians had already voted early -- about 60 percent ahead of the same point in 2022, according to VoteHub's 2026 Early Vote Tracker, built with the L2 voter file. Tennessee's early vote is up 62 percent. South Carolina passed its entire 2022 early-voting total in a little over six days -- nearly 564,000 ballots, a record. In Louisiana, black turnout is pacing at rates rarely seen since 2008, the last time a presidential-level wave pulled the state's electorate forward. Michael McDonald, the University of Florida professor who has been counting early votes since Florida made that a full-time job, reported Sunday that early turnout across six Southern states is running strongest among black and Hispanic voters. Bloomberg's summary put the mechanism in one line: black turnout surging in the South as the voting-rights fallout lands. The fallout has a name and a date. On April 29, the Supreme Court decided 'Louisiana v. Callais', 6-3, with Justice Alito writing for the majority and Justice Kagan dissenting for the three Democratic appointees. The Court held that Louisiana's second majority-Black congressional district -- created to comply with Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act -- was an unconstitutional racial gerrymander. Section 2, as the majority reinterpreted it, requires a strong inference of intentional discrimination, not merely discriminatory effect: the intent standard Congress expressly rejected when it amended the Act in 1982. The NAACP Legal Defense Fund called it an evisceration of the section. Around 140 House districts nationwide are majority-minority; the decision put the logic behind many of them on notice. Then came the number that should interest anyone who cares about voters rather than narratives. VoteHub's analysis of majority-Black Black Belt counties found their turnout edge grew from 1.1 points in the elections before the ruling to 5.9 points in the elections after it. Nothing about the mechanics of voting changed on April 29. The information did. That is the observation, and I want to state the opinion under it plainly: it is a good thing to have more informed voters. Not "voters who agree with me" -- that is the definition every campaign, church bulletin, and cable hit quietly uses. I mean the inconvenient, symmetric version: citizens who know what happened and vote anyway. An informed electorate is the only constituency that cannot be owned. It votes against its informers as readily as with them, banks its own conclusions, and shows up in numbers that embarrass everyone's models. If a party finds informed voters threatening, the finding is the confession. What happened in the Black Belt this fall is information discipline at its purest. A long opinion with footnotes about illustrative maps and Gingles preconditions became, within weeks, required reading in the places it was actually about. The chain was not mysterious: the ruling, then the county explainer, then the barbershop, then the church social hall, then the early-vote line. Nobody had to be convinced the matter was urgent; the Court had already ruled on the weight of their votes. When information arrives with your name attached, consumption is not a problem. People read what assesses them. There is also a register of history worth naming without melodrama. This is an electorate that has been made to re-read its own eligibility more often than any other in America: the Fifteenth Amendment in 1870, the Act in 1965, Shelby County's gutting of preclearance in 2013, 'Callais' in 2026. Each time the status was reopened, the response eventually showed up in the poll books. That is not grievance; it is a discipline -- arguably the most consistently informed habit in American political life. The textbooks say voters are supposed to study the rules. Only one group of voters has had to study the rules about whether they may vote, and has done the homework every time. Two honest caveats, because a surge is not a theorem. Turnout is not the same as being informed; mobilization can ride the same bus as education. Early votes are banked, not won -- McDonald himself cautions that the composition of the early electorate does not guarantee the composition of the final one, and North Carolina's lagging mail ballots keep the 2022 comparisons fuzzier than the headlines suggest. And being informed is not a season; it is a practice. The unphotogenic elections -- school boards, county commissions, the off-years where the next map and the next ruling get drafted -- are where this syllabus either stays open or quietly closes. But on the main point I will take the cheerful position without apology: a voter who read the ruling before voting is the system working , wherever they land on the ballot. Informed voters are not a partisan asset. They are an operational hazard to everyone who preferred them confused, and the republic has no better friends than that. My pieces usually end asking "Who decided?" -- a question about choices made over everyone's heads, in rooms with the good lighting. This time the ledger reads differently. The Court decided the syllabus. The parties decided the venues. But a 4.8-point swing in the Black Belt's turnout edge was decided nowhere but the early-vote lines themselves. For once, the answer is printed where everyone can check it, one name at a time: they did. Thanks for reading! # **Trump credits his endorsement for Netanyahu 's election comeback**
President Donald Trump said his endorsement helped fuel a late surge for Netanyahu's bloc, which partial results showed closing in on a parliamentary majority with 57 of 120 Knesset seats, reversing early exit polls that had favored the opposition.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/7a77c5fa-0f7e-41bf-bd7d-bf70eeb8b0a9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

* **The political developments come as U.S. officials reportedly prepare Gulf allies for a possible major military operation against Iran** after the midterms, with Trump declining to confirm plans but suggesting further strikes remain possible while accusing Iran of stalling talks until after the U.S. election.

# **Cuban diplomat expelled from US after altercation with American official at UN**
U.S. Ambassador Mike Waltz said a Cuban diplomat, identified as Richard Tur de la Concepcion, **[will be expelled after allegedly shoving an American official](https://substack.com/redirect/39821bf5-1586-454b-ad54-653490cc635e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** who was filming a heated exchange between Waltz and Cuba's foreign minister on the UN General Assembly floor Tuesday.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/3c784b06-000e-4412-9490-d59822d34dd1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* **Waltz accused Cuba of using the UN as a "propaganda platform"** ahead of the annual vote condemning the U.S. embargo, highlighting alleged corruption among Cuban elites, including photos of Fidel Castro and current President Miguel Diaz-Canel wearing expensive watches while citizens face hardship.
* **Cuban officials pushed back, accusing the U.S. of spreading lies** to justify economic aggression against the island. The UN is set to vote Wednesday on its 34th consecutive resolution condemning the embargo, which passed with 165 countries in favor last year.

Kathy Hochul told Politico she's eager to see Democrats retake the House and ideally the Senate, saying congressional oversight could **[use investigations, hearings, and subpoenas](https://substack.com/redirect/715f5d5f-0f5e-402b-9d18-ce1540c589e9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** to scrutinize what she called Trump administration corruption and counter his "flood the zone" strategy.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/715f5d5f-0f5e-402b-9d18-ce1540c589e9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

If you've been following what's happening in Minnesota, here's where we're at now:

**We won 't be that team.**

But we're FAR from throwing in the towel.
Now that we're in the home stretch, your direct support to me and this movement becomes even more important.
Truth be told, it'd be a disaster if we lost you, Fellow American.

**WORSHIP IS OUR SUPERPOWER**
---
Before We Head to the Ballot Box, We Must Return to the Altar.
---
| | Something is shaking in America. And something is shaking across the nations of the earth. Political tensions are rising. Elections are dividing families, churches, and communities. Wars and rumors of wars dominate the headlines. Economic uncertainty hangs over households. Fear, confusion, and anxiety seem to be spreading faster than hope. And as we approach another consequential election, I believe the Church must remember something we have too often forgotten:**WORSHIP IS OUR SUPERPOWER.** Our hope has never rested in a political party, a presidential candidate, or the outcome of an election. Our hope is in the King of Kings, whose throne is never threatened by earthly turmoil. That doesn’t mean elections are unimportant. They matter deeply. The decisions made by our elected leaders affect our families, our communities, and future generations. Voting is a meaningful responsibility in a free society, and I encourage every eligible American to participate prayerfully, thoughtfully, and with conviction. **But before we head to the ballot box, clean_body: | | | | | WORSHIP IS OUR SUPERPOWER Before We Head to the Ballot Box, We Must Return to the Altar. | | Something is shaking in America. And something is shaking across the nations of the earth. Political tensions are rising. Elections are dividing families, churches, and communities. Wars and rumors of wars dominate the headlines. Economic uncertainty hangs over households. Fear, confusion, and anxiety seem to be spreading faster than hope. And as we approach another consequential election, I believe the Church must remember something we have too often forgotten:WORSHIP IS OUR SUPERPOWER. Our hope has never rested in a political party, a presidential candidate, or the outcome of an election. Our hope is in the King of Kings, whose throne is never threatened by earthly turmoil. That doesn’t mean elections are unimportant. They matter deeply. The decisions made by our elected leaders affect our families, our communities, and future generations. Voting is a meaningful responsibility in a free society, and I encourage every eligible American to participate prayerfully, thoughtfully, and with conviction. body:
Tomorrow, we take off. Here’s how to make sure The Tennessee Flyover lands in your inbox.

| | |
---
You're officially part of _The Tennessee Flyover_ Crew. Welcome aboard! ✈️ We're glad you're here. Starting tomorrow, you can expect _The Tennessee Flyover_ in your inbox each morning--a quick, engaging rundown of the Tennessee stories worth knowing, along with the biggest national headlines impacting the Volunteer State. It's designed to give you the important stuff without taking up your whole morning. And yes, **it 's free.** Want to see what you signed up for? [You can read our latest Tennessee edition here.](https://email.editor.thetennesseeflyover.com/c/eJx0zz1uhDAQQOHT2N0ie_yDXbhIQ7dpU6IBD4slAys8Icrto6TO9k-f9D7u4x1LLfvjHTdKzMv42egcQYG_aXWDIHOaQEe0s6Sk-2h0DAqCXJOJ6KY8WxXJBKspOBWiAZ99dL2zKEv6ZbSCoK0xNnT94gkn52d0CmEhYRXlwsfZ8UpM-06tES31-7jo7OZjkzWtzM8mzJuAQcDwohMwVGRqLM-Un1-l1tJ8L6x6bFjqn8T_zl0JfgIAAP__kNJQ5Q) Before we send you on your way, we have one small favor to ask.
### Help us make sure _The Tennessee Flyover_ actually lands in your inbox
Email providers sometimes have a mind of their own, especially when you've just subscribed to something new. Taking a minute to tell your inbox you _want_ to hear from us can help make sure tomorrow's _Tennessee Flyover_ doesn't get lost along the way. **The easiest thing you can do?** Hit reply to this email and let us know you got it. Even a quick "Got it!" will do. Then, depending on which email service you use, here's one more step you can take: **Gmail**
* **On your phone:** Tap the three dots (...) in the top-right corner, choose "Move to," then select "Primary." If you don't see Primary as an option, you're already set.
* **On desktop:** Go back to your inbox and drag this email into the "Primary" tab.

**Apple Mail**
* Tap our email address at the top of this email (next to "From:" on mobile), then select "Add to VIP."

**AOL Mail**
* Select "Contacts," then "New Contact." Add [news@editor.thetennesseeflyover.com](mailto:news@editor.thetennesseeflyover.com) and save it as a contact.

**Outlook**
* Hover over our email address at the top of this email, click the three dots, choose "Add to Outlook Contacts," then click "Save" or "Create."

**Use something else?** [You can find instructions for your email provider here.](https://email.editor.thetennesseeflyover.com/c/eJx0z7GOhCAQgOGngU4DI4IWFNfY7bVXGpBBJ0HdyOxu7u0vd_Vt_-dL_q_bfAtU6Fg_w46eOc-PitcMCmyjVQODTD6CHoNZJHrtxk6Pg4JBbj7G3ulkMRrTmxBcVrrrIS1uNOBsdpL8L6MVDNp0nRlaly2G2Nsl9CpARmEUJuLzanlDxuPAWhFz-T6feLXLucviN-Z7Fd2HgEnA9KYTML02YixUmY61WR-UUMAkL5_uLyqFqnXCqHUPVP5g_vf16eEnAAD__wDkVss) And that's it. You're ready for takeoff. One last thing: **we really do want to hear from you.** If you have feedback, a Tennessee story you think we should cover, or just want to tell us what you think of _The Tennessee Flyover_ , email our Editor anytime at****[editor@thetennesseeflyover.com](mailto:editor@thetennesseeflyover.com). Thanks for joining us. We'll see you in your inbox!

**WEDNESDAY, OCTOBER 28, 2026**
**George Washington | Letter to his nephew, March 23, 1789**
"It is therefore absolutely necessary if you mean to make any figure upon the stage, that you should take the first steps right."
Writing to his young nephew, George Washington offered the guidance of age and experience. He understood that conduct could shape traits of character that might endure throughout life.
We often choose without understanding how far our actions may reach. Those who have lived longer have a responsibility to teach; those who hear have a responsibility to consider that counsel.
How do we choose rightly when we cannot yet see where our choices lead?
Perhaps there is no certainty to be found before we begin. We listen, we consider, we choose--and sometimes only time reveals what we could not see at the start.
**Pause.**
**Breath.**
**Look Deeper.**
**Refuel.**
**Welcome to Sweet Ground.**
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/61a16606-ee0f-4ce4-b6f4-4ac11640022e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**A SWEET GROUND INVITATION**
In Sweet Ground, we reflect on the people who shape us, the choices we make, what we must sometimes unlearn, and what we carry forward.
Now, I would like to hear from you.
Is there a moment from your own life that has stayed with you? Something a parent or grandparent taught you, a conversation you never forgot, a lesson you understood only years later, or an ordinary moment that turned out not to be so ordinary?
**Share your Sweet Ground moment in the comments.** A few words are enough. A memory, a story, even a photograph with a few words about what it means to you.
There is no right answer and no perfect story. Just something from your life that you carry with you.
I would love to hear it.

name: Darline Graham
subject: Breaking it down
body:
We have 6 days left. Let me explain what's at stake. |
---

Fellow Patriot -

Here's a breakdown of our race ... _by the numbers_.

**$9 million:**
This is how much Annie Andrews raised last quarter.
I got into this race long after she was already raising millions of dollars from liberals all over the country. She has the support of Hollywood stars like Star Wars' Mark Hamill and Roseanne's John Goodman.

**3 months:**
How long I've been in this race.
I did not seek this moment, Fellow Patriot. I never thought I'd be in this position. Politics was Lindsey's thing. But when President Trump asked me to run for a full Senate term, I knew I had to answer the call to, once again, serve the people of South Carolina.

Since entering, I am running my third statewide campaign in just three months. I know so many of you have been so generous to help me, but it's taken its toll. Our campaign is running on fumes.

**RCP Average: +2.7:**
**Darline Graham: 48%**
**Annie Andrews: 45.3%**
This is the average of all the recent polls in the South Carolina Senate races. We're only up by 2.7%.

Annie Andrews and her liberal Super PACs have spent millions attacking me, spreading lies about my family and me. She's also lying about where she stands on the issues. She's wearing a "moderate mask" that will disappear IF she's elected to the Senate to stand with Chuck Schumer, James Talarico, and Abdul El-Sayed.

**6 Days:**
_That's all we have left before Election Day._
Time isn't on our side, Fellow Patriot. **[To finish out this race, I need you by my side.](http://links.conservativesdefendingfreedom.com/u/click?_t=91d01aa68bbe4105984439520ca0f0af&_m=6e3e72139a154c5fa1e6537f1a31609d&_e=hxJ6KsKhUTm2bkiZTrYOuXOQkzK-nYoDu0DRRZ3UiYa8mQHa3DE7upU2WrS6VxQPUVz827lpQeddyLnsK7RY9yFtvpZC-fv9Bs--6zmFLOWARzMLMlOQ8fD29w2UiX_LYCGI4H_v_7HPaVygPgdMWnLTgoXsMBS-HWLy9fW7hrPFEWdXPp-woNJN1-OrQo5HQS7e5tKJnodC-BvNk7PY3-fu8dszrbBEpETkPFN5QannrxLvukGO47jM0UWUihgsg0vlkScDV6zWiQqJY8eiGkAWnWxf3XMIlPTiT7WxMMluklLP22rSkDyUO8cdIAKpEV_pSjnzGIfWQziv0loKSg1E21i43OUMjXC2qddLbJ-qmCb3KQ0CGMx45FknYrW_Q3fIZgUB457mmBOorax2PdbeUXfoE1cPW4SosumxgJeDbR92BJc9zKXOL2uTEA0X2hsbDQAMtic9gfXaCe0eiLBSGxhzrZrBJSBfP3G2S6dJS7OZrkzqZZyy5wrbZm4Gtx5ok5TWHpLl7LVgBRfBCIW_o47SeW_65lnfSK5rHjUln3yeoYdW-Ven6-7gv200bxSMXNCw8c-6kffC-I2F3iV8fIvxDELKkgGKkPViLTB5KUFiMlQGjeQNJ6prOCaQe55pMWMNYlunmIe46jWam1wZN5HU93EV2R8eWf_ABz6T7WyKgnw-u9f02AroZhB9DINSjt9gbg-LvBrlC-HVWiRHr8PYqe0kJSZHP4nu6MY%3D)**

President Trump needs a Senate majority that will stand with him, and South Carolina's seat is on the line. The Democrats are throwing everything they have at this race because they know a single seat could decide who controls the Senate.

I can't win this alone. I'm counting on grassroots conservatives like you, not big-money donors, to get us across the finish line. **[Will you chip in $10 or even $20 right now?](http://links.conservativesdefendingfreedom.com/u/click?_t=91d01aa68bbe4105984439520ca0f0af&_m=6e3e72139a154c5fa1e6537f1a31609d&_e=hxJ6KsKhUTm2bkiZTrYOuXOQkzK-nYoDu0DRRZ3UiYa8mQHa3DE7upU2WrS6VxQPUVz827lpQeddyLnsK7RY9yFtvpZC-fv9Bs--6zmFLOWARzMLMlOQ8fD29w2UiX_LYCGI4H_v_7HPaVygPgdMWnLTgoXsMBS-HWLy9fW7hrPFEWdXPp-woNJN1-OrQo5HQS7e5tKJnodC-BvNk7PY3-fu8dszrbBEpETkPFN5QannrxLvukGO47jM0UWUihgslHqJozQvOWZqQ-GZOLoaKtc6MkjPefKnHs81slD1q5h853fsKbR_Ol3aNUuvikAL55rjiF28PNFXc0pGk3R0ccr6hp2fecxtOAGlrp25TM9BIM5yglokQq8xZTRiPsBosBIgymbBwsyBhfAuxCy6G3U62yszszBxH1tqqw-iwp-tbAPIHPVPFymqwwaw4DLtu16U4DsIYIGClFiMN9znKTHK2Y3DTTfeMr2C_ZAmMJoBgtFXsi1mg_1Er4GNQhjvBJIBAtF9AdpD-jemdQM1xa_YubHIAX7v6P44kSTLOyL_63X28puz2fXhrUdp_jW4Lniuxz1tvfjZjXBBpZDs3xrxGVcq9z2TgQpig_Nk-1enq2Oo2paArXPm1fDLmO_DjhEJmuHtKLCYZgF43Md4NlyaDiPtRlz2D52llOt-UOTABDzFn79GykPmZihKLN_dFSBwf83FEs5eOpuxUkv-1WGhbzCuq2FBPXum3orDW9s%3D)**

It's Chris.
In a few hours, I'll walk onto the WMUR debate stage and face John Sununu for the last time before Election Day.
My team and I are in the final stretch of prep, and I wanted to write to you directly before it starts: **[If you can swing it, will you chip in $15 before I take the stage tonight?](https://substack.com/redirect/ab15a4c6-f4ef-444a-941f-ae2e94a62f55?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[ DONATE](https://substack.com/redirect/ab15a4c6-f4ef-444a-941f-ae2e94a62f55?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Here's why tonight matters: **This is our last debate before the election, and one of our final opportunities to show Granite Staters exactly who John Sununu is.**
1. **John Sununu went to Washington 25 years ago and voted with Big Pharma against lower drug prices and for a $700 billion Wall Street bailout.** Then he made up to $35 million after cashing in with those same industries.
2. **Sununu is the lead architect of a plan to privatize Social Security, gamble it on the stock market, add trillions of dollars to our debt, and allow Wall Street to charge fees on the backs of New Hampshire workers.** Then he was just caught on tape saying that he is willing to privatize Social Security _again_ if he goes back to the Senate.
3. **If elected Sununu would rubber stamp Donald Trump 's reckless agenda. **The same agenda that has given us skyrocketing oil, gas, and diesel prices; endless war; and reckless tariffs that cost Granite State households $5,300 more.

John Sununu has Trump's personal endorsement and the full backing of national Republicans who are spending more than $66 million to get him elected and buy this seat.
**We don 't have any of that.**
I don't take a dime of corporate PAC money. What powers this campaign is a movement of Granite Staters and grassroots supporters who chip in what they can when they can, and I want to walk onto that stage tonight with all of that momentum on my side.

**I called it. From the sidelines.**
For months, I've warned that Connecticut's affordability debate could lead to more taxes, more state control over education, and fewer decisions left to our towns.
I've raised concerns about highway tolls, regional education, and the possibility of a statewide property tax. I brought them up again during my debate with my opponent who has had 8 years of executing bad plays that cost Greenwich billions.
My impression? He cringed.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/f860d62e-ecb3-4f43-bc64-ae5c15ddf992?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Jonathan Goldstein Remarks on CT Mirror Article - with clip from debate.
[Pledge your support](https://substack..ChkDbasZ-LyB_EQCMJHbhwf5HhFPKra4sHJYNPPFhSg?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=222497597)
[Share](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=1454853&post_id=222497597&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MjIyNDk3NTk3LCJpYXQiOjE3OTMyMDAyNDYsImV4cCI6MTc5NTc5MjI0NiwiaXNzIjoicHViLTE0NTQ4NTMiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.pnDAimYj6gHDu3XAYJT4FEMXHMs81QLzFSMCPMBm43M)
Then, on October 26, the CT Mirror published this headline:
**["Citizens group wants tolls, tax on rich to finance property tax relief."](https://substack.com/redirect/138535f7-4059-45a6-b4fb-26221370a7c1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
The Connecticut Citizens' Assembly recommended highway tolls, higher income taxes on wealthy residents, and incentives for school regionalization.
These are recommendations, not enacted laws. A statewide property tax was not among them. But the proposals raise questions about taxation, school funding, and local control that I've been discussing throughout this campaign.
**Are we lowering the cost of living, or just finding another way to collect the money?**
Connecticut families already pay income taxes, sales taxes, gasoline and diesel taxes, and local property taxes. They also face high electricity costs and Public Benefits Charges on their utility bills.
The assembly's proposals include eliminating municipal motor vehicle taxes and shifting special education costs to the state. Those ideas deserve serious examination.
But taxpayers need to see the full equation.
If Hartford takes money out of your left pocket and puts some back in your right pocket, how much have you actually saved?
**Tax relief should reduce the burden, not rearrange the bill.**
Before creating new taxes, I want to examine what government spends, what residents receive, and whether existing resources can be used more effectively.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/9e477942-dd53-457b-899c-c0dd83742b26?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
## Eight Years in the Game. What Are the Results?
My opponent has represented Greenwich for eight years as a member of Hartford's majority party.
He points to an additional $8 million brought back to our community and spends thousands to send you a mailer to brag about it.
I welcome every dollar. But Greenwich residents contribute billions in state taxes, and I believe we should examine whether our town receives a fair return and the answer is NO. **Talk to any parent**.
Consider school construction.
[Fairfield has qualified for reimbursement rates as high as 75% on a school project, while Greenwich has been looking at approximately 20% for Central Middle School.](https://substack.com/redirect/bb539f53-e2c4-48a0-8995-9a1a1694222d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
The projects operate under different reimbursement rules, but those differences deserve scrutiny. I want to pursue every available opportunity for fairer funding and examine whether the state's system adequately recognizes Greenwich's needs.
**Eight years. Billions sent. A few million returned.**
We've had eight years to evaluate the current approach.
**What would another two years change?**
To me, representation isn't about access, seniority, or appearances at press conferences. It's about understanding the issues, influencing decisions, and producing results.
## You Don't Have to Control the Game to Make a Difference
If elected, I'll likely be in the minority in Hartford. But being in the minority doesn't mean being silent.
Have you ever heard the kids at the kids' table? **Sometimes they make so much noise the grown-ups have no choice but to listen.**
**I 'd rather be heard from the minority table than sit quietly with the majority.**
As an attorney and construction professional, I've negotiated with people who held more leverage than I did. I've learned that **you don 't have to control the room to influence the outcome.** You need to know the facts, make your case, and challenge decisions that don't make sense.
That's what I'll bring to Hartford: tough questions, practical alternatives, and a willingness to work across party lines.
With a supermajority, a legislator can vote "no" and still watch a bill pass. The real work happens before that vote.
**I 'm not looking for a hall pass to vote "no" after the outcome is decided. I'm going to Hartford to help change the outcome.**
**Greenwich doesn 't just need a seat at the table. It needs a voice that can't be ignored.**
### _The Kids ' Table Still Has a Voice - _Our Schools. Our Taxes. Our Decisions For Our Community.
The discussion about school regionalization deserves particular attention.
The citizens' assembly recommended incentives for regional cooperation, not mandatory school consolidation. Shared services that save money and improve education may be worthwhile.
But I oppose using state funding to pressure municipalities into surrendering control over their schools.
> I also oppose a statewide property tax that could move important decisions about local taxation farther from the residents paying the bills.
Greenwich already funds its schools through substantial local property taxes. Any proposal to restructure education funding should be examined for its effect on school quality, local accountability, and the total tax burden.
**Greenwich shouldn 't have to buy back its independence from Hartford, especially when we are already paying for it.**
And when the state imposes a mandate, the state should pay for it.
## What I Want to Accomplish
My priorities remain **Affordability, Beaches, and Local Control.**
On affordability, I want to pursue a temporary suspension of gasoline and diesel taxes, address the Public Benefits Charge through transparent state budgeting, oppose additional taxes that increase the overall burden, and fight for fairer school funding.
On beaches, I want to address sewage pollution in Long Island Sound and the infrastructure problems contributing to recurring closures.
On local control, I want Greenwich to retain meaningful authority over its schools, zoning, housing, and infrastructure.
These are practical issues that affect household budgets, businesses, children's education, and our community's future.
I've spent my career working with contracts, construction projects, budgets, and complicated problems. I know that identifying a problem is only the beginning. You have to develop a workable solution and persuade others to act.
That's what I want to do in Hartford.
## Put Me in the Game.
I've spent this campaign studying Hartford's proposals, raising concerns, and offering alternatives without having a vote in the General Assembly.
I've been calling the plays from the sidelines with an entertaining social media presence.
But there's a difference between identifying problems and having the opportunity to work on legislation.
I'm ready for that responsibility.
And if I end up in the minority, I won't confuse that with having no voice.
After all, have you ever heard how much noise the kids can make at the kids' table?
Sometimes even the grown-ups have to stop and listen.
**I 've called it from the sidelines. I'm ready to do the work on the field.**
**Put me in, Coach. I 'm ready to represent Greenwich. Don't Let Hartford Push Us Around Anymore!**
_Not Red. Not Blue. Just Greenwich._
**Jonathan Goldstein -- Row 4B**

Here's what I intend to do if I get one. | | ---|---|--- | | | Forwarded this email? ? for more The Goldstein Substack - A Father-Son Publication Dr. Goldstein is Running for Congress and his page can be found Higher taxes. Highway tolls. Regional education. I've been warning about these issues without a vote in Hartford. Here's what I intend to do if I get one. | | | Oct 28| | | ∙| | Guest post ---|---|--- | | | | | | | | | | | | I called it. From the sidelines. For months, I've warned that Connecticut's affordability debate could lead to more taxes, more state control over education, and fewer decisions left to our towns. I've raised concerns about highway tolls, regional education, and the possibility of a statewide property tax. I brought them up again during my debate with my opponent who has had 8 years of executing bad plays that cost Greenwich billions. My impression? He cringed. Jonathan Goldstein Remarks on CT Mirror Article - with clip from debate. Then, on October 26, the CT Mirror published this headline: The Connecticut Citizens' Assembly recommended highway tolls, higher income taxes on wealthy residents, and incentives for school regionalization. These are recommendations, not enacted laws. A statewide property tax was not among them. But the proposals raise questions about taxation, school funding, and local control that I've been discussing throughout this campaign. Are we lowering the cost of living, or just finding another way to collect the money? Connecticut families already pay income taxes, sales taxes, gasoline and diesel taxes, and local property taxes. They also face high electricity costs and Public Benefits Charges on their utility bills. The assembly's proposals include eliminating municipal motor vehicle taxes and shifting special education costs to the state. Those ideas deserve serious examination. But taxpayers need to see the full equation. If Hartford takes money out of your left pocket and puts some back in your right pocket, how much have you actually saved? Tax relief should reduce the burden, not rearrange the bill. Before creating new taxes, I want to examine what government spends, what residents receive, and whether existing resources can be used more effectively. | | ---|---|--- Eight Years in the Game. What Are the Results? My opponent has represented Greenwich for eight years as a member of Hartford's majority party. He points to an additional $8 million brought back to our community and spends thousands to send you a mailer to brag about it. I welcome every dollar. But Greenwich residents contribute billions in state taxes, and I believe we should examine whether our town receives a fair return and the answer is NO. Talk to any parent. Consider school construction. The projects operate under different reimbursement rules, but those differences deserve scrutiny. I want to pursue every available opportunity for fairer funding and examine whether the state's system adequately recognizes Greenwich's needs. Eight years. Billions sent. A few million returned. We've had eight years to evaluate the current approach. What would another two years change? To me, representation isn't about access, seniority, or appearances at press conferences. It's about understanding the issues, influencing decisions, and producing results. You Don't Have to Control the Game to Make a Difference If elected, I'll likely be in the minority in Hartford. But being in the minority doesn't mean being silent. Have you ever heard the kids at the kids' table? Sometimes they make so much noise the grown-ups have no choice but to listen. I 'd rather be heard from the minority table than sit quietly with the majority. As an attorney and construction professional, I've negotiated with people who held more leverage than I did. I've learned that you don 't have to control the room to influence the outcome. You need to know the facts, make your case, and challenge decisions that don't make sense. That's what I'll bring to Hartford: tough questions, practical alternatives, and a willingness to work across party lines. With a supermajority, a legislator can vote "no" and still watch a bill pass. The real work happens before that vote. I 'm not looking for a hall pass to vote "no" after the outcome is decided. I'm going to Hartford to help change the outcome. Greenwich doesn 't just need a seat at the table. It needs a voice that can't be ignored. The Kids ' Table Still Has a Voice - Our Schools. Our Taxes. Our Decisions For Our Community. The discussion about school regionalization deserves particular attention. The citizens' assembly recommended incentives for regional cooperation, not mandatory school consolidation. Shared services that save money and improve education may be worthwhile. But I oppose using state funding to pressure municipalities into surrendering control over their schools. I also oppose a statewide property tax that could move important decisions about local taxation farther from the residents paying the bills. Greenwich already funds its schools through substantial local property taxes. Any proposal to restructure education funding should be examined for its effect on school quality, local accountability, and the total tax burden. Greenwich shouldn 't have to buy back its independence from Hartford, especially when we are already paying for it. And when the state imposes a mandate, the state should pay for it. What I Want to Accomplish My priorities remain Affordability, Beaches, and Local Control. On affordability, I want to pursue a temporary suspension of gasoline and diesel taxes, address the Public Benefits Charge through transparent state budgeting, oppose additional taxes that increase the overall burden, and fight for fairer school funding. On beaches, I want to address sewage pollution in Long Island Sound and the infrastructure problems contributing to recurring closures. On local control, I want Greenwich to retain meaningful authority over its schools, zoning, housing, and infrastructure. These are practical issues that affect household budgets, businesses, children's education, and our community's future. I've spent my career working with contracts, construction projects, budgets, and complicated problems. I know that identifying a problem is only the beginning. You have to develop a workable solution and persuade others to act. That's what I want to do in Hartford. Put Me in the Game. I've spent this campaign studying Hartford's proposals, raising concerns, and offering alternatives without having a vote in the General Assembly. I've been calling the plays from the sidelines with an entertaining social media presence. But there's a difference between identifying problems and having the opportunity to work on legislation. I'm ready for that responsibility. And if I end up in the minority, I won't confuse that with having no voice. After all, have you ever heard how much noise the kids can make at the kids' table? Sometimes even the grown-ups have to stop and listen. I 've called it from the sidelines. I'm ready to do the work on the field. Put me in, Coach. I 'm ready to represent Greenwich. Don't Let Hartford Push Us Around Anymore! Not Red. Not Blue. Just Greenwich. Here is what I know about my uncle:
When nobody stops him, he keeps pushing.
When he feels that void, he stokes conflict at home and abroad to fill it.
And when he is challenged, he gets reckless.
He tests every limit and counts on fear, exhaustion, and silence.
We cannot give him any of those things. Most importantly, we must elect the kinds of leaders with the courage and integrity to stand up to my uncle and the entire machine of corporate interests, dark money donors, and MAGA yes-men enabling him.

On November 8th, 2022, after a difficult, expensive, and hard-fought reelection campaign, I called my opponent to offer my concession and congratulations.

It wasn't a pleasant call to make. But I've never second-guessed the decisions that led me there.

In Congress, I served on the January 6th Committee, knowing full well it could cost me my seat. That cycle, outside far-right groups spent $6,059,677 against me. Add a national environment that was brutal for frontline Democrats, and I came up short.

**For me, the worst outcome isn’t losing a fight. It’s going down with no fight at all.**

So I'm back, running to win this seat back from Jen Kiggans, because I can't sit on the sidelines and watch our country descend into chaos.

Jen Kiggans called Elon Musk's DOGE cuts "so necessary," even as they hit Hampton Roads hard. Musk's super PAC is spending to keep her in office. Trump has spent $1.5M on ads against me. # Iran
* **Qatar presents new proposal to end Iran war:** Qatari mediators [presented](https://substack.com/redirect/1bda8a74-e2ec-4a90-9c50-30dfe80e9029?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Iran with a new seven-day proposal to end the eight-month U.S.-Israeli war. A senior Iranian official said the proposal consisted of "unacceptable ideas" and that it was "not an offer," according to Reuters.
* The proposal, reportedly approved by the U.S., outlined daily confidence-building measures by both sides, potentially beginning early next week, with several countries serving as guarantors, according to an official briefed on the negotiations. Qatari mediators presented it to Iran on Sunday, the official added.
* Washington insists that nuclear negotiations begin immediately, while Iran demands an end to the U.S. blockade and the lifting of oil sanctions before beginning those negotiations.
* The diplomatic push comes amid renewed threats of military escalation. The U.S. [warned](https://substack.com/redirect/9a5864bc-3fb7-4639-96ce-dd85948f5d28?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) several Gulf Arab states to prepare for a "short, intense military campaign" following next week's U.S. midterm elections, according to the Wall Street Journal.
* Meanwhile, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi [warned](https://substack.com/redirect/89b1ab82-dd7e-4923-b4dc-c3905404221e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that the "devastating impact on international markets of any Israel-instigated military misadventure" in the Persian Gulf remains a major concern for global energy producers and consumers.
* **Iran denies involvement in alleged assassination plot in Kuwait after three sentenced to death:** Iran's embassy in Kuwait [rejected](https://substack.com/redirect/6d477e75-b7c3-4961-99ce-8b787460ad73?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) accusations that an Iranian national was involved in a plot to assassinate senior Kuwaiti officials, saying on Wednesday that the individual had not been in Kuwait for the past decade.
* The statement came after a Kuwaiti court sentenced three defendants to death on Monday, including Iranian national Abdulreza Dehqani, and two Kuwaiti nationals, while eight others received five-year prison sentences. Kuwaiti prosecutors accused the defendants of espionage for Iran and Lebanon's Hezbollah and of plotting to assassinate the First Deputy Prime Minister, the Interior Minister, and other senior officials.
* **U.S. military spending on Iran war surpasses $47 billion, up more than 25% since July:** The U.S. military has [spent](https://substack.com/redirect/62d9cb80-c57b-4e83-bf0e-de19564e5ada?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) more than $47 billion on its war against Iran, over 25% higher than the Pentagon's $37.5 billion estimate in July, according to internal War Department figures obtained by Reuters.
* The latest estimate includes more than $29 billion to replace expended munitions and over $6 billion to replace lost military equipment, including aircraft and drones.
* The figures do not clearly account for the potentially enormous cost of repairing U.S. military bases damaged by Iranian missile and drone attacks.
* **IAEA says no evidence Iran has rebuilt nuclear facilities damaged in U.S.-Israeli strikes:** The head of the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) [said](https://substack.com/redirect/b849b798-73f5-4887-9042-d4317bb89a9a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that there was no activity suggesting Iran has attempted to repair or rebuild nuclear facilities damaged by U.S. and Israeli attacks in 2025 and 2026.
* "Since June 2025, we have not identified any activity to repair or reconstruct any of the facilities damaged in the military attacks of 2025 and 2026," Director General Rafael Grossi told the UN Security Council on Tuesday. But he stressed that the agency still needs access to verify the facilities' condition and account for previously declared nuclear material, including 440 kilograms of highly enriched uranium.
* **Gulf states reportedly push diplomatic deal involving Iran, Yemen, and Hormuz:** Gulf states are [developing](https://substack.com/redirect/e1e5244c-b146-42f7-be4a-78fe3c694de6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a diplomatic deal to avert another U.S.-Iran war that involves the Strait of Hormuz, Yemen, and a new regional security framework, The Guardian reported.
* Iran's Mohsen Rezaei met Ansarallah's ambassador a day after senior Saudi, Turkish, and Pakistani officials visited Tehran.
* Iran could sway Ansarallah, potentially facilitating a settlement short of total military victory--expelling Saudi Arabia from the country. Ansarallah is demanding an end to Saudi Arabia's air and naval blockade.
* According to The Guardian, Iran "successfully prevented discussion of its nuclear programme" at the Tehran meeting, instead steering talks toward a regional security arrangement that would include Iran and Gulf states while reducing or ending the U.S. military presence in the Middle East.
* **UAE closes all Sharjah beaches as tanker oil spill spreads across northern emirates:** Authorities in Sharjah closed all beaches across the city following an oil spill from a damaged tanker in nearby waters, describing the decision as a "proactive precautionary measure."
* The closure comes after dozens of beaches and coastal areas across Umm Al Quwain and Ras Al Khaimah have been shut down in recent days, with satellite imagery showing the spill stretching across the UAE's northern coastline.
* Experts told Reuters the oil was leaking from the Panama-flagged Gem No. 2, a tanker reportedly struck by an unidentified projectile last month.

# Palestine
* **Four Palestinians killed in Israeli strikes across Gaza:** An**** Israeli [airstrike](https://substack.com/redirect/78877914-c4bf-4c62-92a3-adf01a4192f3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on the Mawasi area of Rafah, southern Gaza, killed three Palestinians and wounded at least 10 on Wednesday, according to WAFA. A**** drone strike in the Mawasi area of Al-Qarara, north of Khan Younis, southern Gaza, killed one Palestinian and wounded several others. Separately, a Palestinian man and his daughter were wounded in an Israeli strike on the Ard Al-Laymoun area south of Khan Younis.
* Over the past 24 hours, Israeli attacks killed three Palestinians--one in a new Israeli attack and two after succumbing to wounds sustained in earlier attacks--and injured 11 others across Gaza, according to the Palestinian Ministry of Health.
* The total recorded death toll since October 7, 2023, is now 74,564 killed, with 175,770 injured. Since October 11, 2025, the first full day of the so-called ceasefire, Israel has killed at least 1,568 Palestinians in Gaza and wounded 5,649, while 845 bodies have been recovered.

* **Israeli forces demolish homes in the occupied West Bank as Hebron assault enters sixth day:**
* **Hebron:** Israeli forces [continued](https://substack.com/redirect/d43c0f1f-4bd5-4623-80be-51ca5814b39f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) their military assault for the sixth consecutive day on Wednesday, sealing off the neighborhoods of Al-Jalda and Deir Baha, raiding homes, destroying property, and converting residential buildings into military outposts, WAFA reported.
* Around 780 families have been affected by the siege, with nearly 5,000 Palestinians forcibly displaced or confined to their homes, according to Hebron Municipality.
* Israeli forces detained approximately 110 Palestinians, including seven children and three women, and subjected hundreds more to field interrogations, according to the Palestinian Prisoners Society.
* **Nablus:** Israeli forces [demolished](https://substack.com/redirect/60b7a87d-0034-4a14-b55c-a1dfc1882373?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) one home and blew up another in Beita after forcing residents to evacuate the western part of the town. In Yasid, north of Nablus, Israeli soldiers beat a Palestinian and his son during a raid, leaving one with a fractured hand.
* **Bethlehem:** Israeli forces [maintained](https://substack.com/redirect/d389614c-7cc4-4590-95e6-9d25fd553f2f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) road closures across the governorate for the sixth consecutive day, blocking access to several towns and villages.
* **Tulkarm:** Israeli forces [arrested](https://substack.com/redirect/39cdfa2f-5a6f-47ae-80c8-b047a4852115?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) four Palestinians, including the journalist and former prisoner Hamza Salama and two of his brothers. An officer in the Palestinian General Intelligence Service, Mohammed Al-Qass, was arrested during a raid on his home.
* **Workers at nearly 50 ports worldwide plan Friday strikes in solidarity with Gaza** : Trade unions at nearly 50 ports worldwide, spanning Mexico, Europe, and India, are [planning](https://substack.com/redirect/5213234c-a9bb-49d5-bc52-9f9b57a3db36?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) strikes and demonstrations on Friday in solidarity with Palestinians in Gaza, demanding an end to Israel's genocide and unrestricted humanitarian aid access, according to Shaher Saad, secretary-general of the Palestinian General Federation of Trade Unions. The actions are being coordinated with the International Transport Workers' Federation.
* **Netanyahu falls short of majority; no clear winner in Israeli elections:** Neither of the two leading political camps have yet secured the 61 seats required to win a parliamentary majority in the 120-member Knesset. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc has secured 53 seats. Opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot's bloc stands at 48 seats. As of 12:34 p.m. local time on Wednesday, 84.5% of ballots were counted, according to preliminary results.
* Palestinian parties are projected to secure 19 seats. Although they have significant leverage given their electoral gains, it is unclear if any opposition bloc would be willing to form a coalition with them to form a majority. Netanyahu openly dismissed the idea, saying, "We must not endanger Israel and establish a government that relies on anti-Zionist Arab parties."
* Meanwhile, U.S. President Donald Trump claimed that his endorsement of Netanyahu "helped him a lot." "It's looking like maybe a stalemate or a win," Trump told reporters.

# Yemen
* **Ansarallah missile hits Aden airport:** An Ansarallah missile reportedly hit Aden International Airport in southern Yemen on Wednesday. Ansarallah military spokesperson Yahya Saree called for the immediate evacuation of the airport, claiming that a Saudi military cargo plane was transporting weapons intended for use against Yemenis.
* The group later repeated the [warning](https://substack.com/redirect/8c3add0f-88c8-4739-b0e8-6f2a273c5801?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), describing it as its "final" call for everyone at the airport to leave immediately.
* The missile reportedly struck the airport before the group issued its warnings, according to a police source cited by AFP.
* **Ansarallah-appointed governor claims most of Yemen 's Taiz is under its control: **The province of Taiz is under the control of Ansarallah, except for parts of Taiz city, the Ansarallah-appointed governor of Taiz Ahmed Al-Masawa [claimed](https://substack.com/redirect/8010d9d6-c2b4-41df-99c3-dbe9dcc36a02?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Tuesday in an interview with Ansarallah's Al-Masirah TV.
* Taiz city, the provincial capital, is still under siege and largely controlled by Saudi-backed government forces.
* Human Rights Watch [said](https://substack.com/redirect/09fd36de-a480-446b-b27d-fcc445cf9c30?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that roads into and out of Taiz city have been "largely blocked by government-affiliated and Houthi forces" since October 1. It also documents Ansarallah forces blowing up the Hayjat Al-Abd road on October 18, the main entry point for food, medicine and fuel.

# Lebanon
* **Israeli forces bombard southern Lebanon towns amid "ceasefire":**
* **Nabatieh:** Israeli artillery shelling [targeted](https://substack.com/redirect/c88b8e19-a1cc-4d82-b747-48d3fdee6c63?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the area between Mifdoun and Zawtar Al-Sharqieh on Wednesday morning, Lebanon's National News Agency reported.
* **Tyre (Sour):** Israeli artillery shelled Mansouri, Majdal Zoun, and surrounding valleys.
* **Marjeyoun:** Israeli forces [caused](https://substack.com/redirect/8a73e4ed-0cb6-4d8e-a4b6-1e3d2a4d0e9a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) two large explosions, one near the cemetery in Khiam and another in the town of Tallouseh on Tuesday.

# U.S. News
* **Man dies in ICE facility in San Diego, the 30th death in ICE detention this year: Roberto Jimenez Gutierrez** , a detainee at ICE's Otay Mesa facility in San Diego, [died](https://substack.com/redirect/e3110582-2ab9-4ab0-9adf-f18183cf377b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) at the facility on Saturday, ICE said on Monday. Gutierrez, a 43-year-old Guatemalan national, was arrested in Escondido and had been in custody since October 9. ICE said that he was in an "assigned safety cell" at the Core Civic-run facility when he died.
* The agency also claimed that Gutierrez was detained in July 2024 after being convicted of selling liquor to a minor and several other arrests without apparent convictions. The local news outlet Daylight San Diego could not locate court records matching ICE's claims. ICE said that a judge ordered him deported to Mexico in 2006.
* **Ambassador Waltz and Cuban Foreign Minister argue on UN floor:** U.S. Ambassador to the UN **Mike Waltz** [clashed](https://substack.com/redirect/c8880908-7fc8-41a2-ad1c-37665d218ccf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) with Cuban Foreign Minister **Bruno Rodr iguez Parrilla** on Tuesday, after Waltz delivered an inflammatory speech criticizing the Cuban government. Rodriguez Parrilla approached the podium during the speech, and Waltz told him to back up, saying that Rodriguez was trying to "intimidate me in the United States of America like he tries to intimidate political prisoners" in Cuba. General Assembly President **Khalilur Rahman** requested that Waltz be allowed to finish his speech before hearing Cuba's point of order. Decorum continued to break down, and Rahman suspended the meeting.
* **Trump again calls for Venezuela to be 51st state:** At an event in Texas on Tuesday, Trump [said](https://substack.com/redirect/d3034a73-b69a-4183-b8f6-9212c4655d07?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that Venezuela should be made part of the United States. "Maybe someday soon, it will become a prosperous 51st state," he said, adding that "instead of a president, we'll have an election for a governor." Addressing the oil tycoon **Harold Hamm** , who was in the crowd, he said, "Let's make it the 51st state." Earlier this year, Trump said that he was "seriously considering" making Venezuela a state. The country's acting president, **Delcy Rodr iguez**, said in May that Venezuela had no plans to become a U.S. state and that it would defend its sovereignty.
* **Rubio adviser Jeremy Lewin leaves State Department ahead of midterms:** **Jeremy Lewin** , the 29-year-old under secretary and director of policy planning at the State Department, [announced](https://substack.com/redirect/6312ae87-783f-490b-8797-51cb09141050?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Tuesday that he was leaving the administration for a job in the private sector. Lewin, a DOGE alum who helped dismantle USAID, led U.S. engagement with Venezuela's **Delcy Rodr iguez**, helped assemble Trump's Venezuela oil deal, and led bilateral talks in Havana with **Ra ul Guillermo Rodriguez Castro**, grandson of **Ra ul Castro**.
* Separately on Tuesday, WIRED reported on Lewin's time at USAID, where for three weeks Lewin essentially ran the agency as if he was its director, canceling lifesaving aid programs and dismissing employees even though he had not signed the paperwork required to work at the agency. The full report from WIRED is available [here](https://substack.com/redirect/3a0ad592-c904-4fec-8400-69bca702cfdf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
* **Grand jury declines to indict Cassidy Hutchinson:** A federal grand jury in Washington on Tuesday [returned](https://substack.com/redirect/61f8dcf8-44e7-4c2e-b327-1f39afe8940a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a "no true bill" on the Justice Department's bid to indict **Cassidy Hutchinson** , the former White House aide who testified against the administration to Congress regarding the January 6 Capitol attack. The DOJ tried to charge Hutchinson with lying to Congress, the New York Times reported. Some DOJ prosecutors were reportedly skeptical of the case, which was led by Trump loyalist **Harmeet Dhillon** , head of the department's civil rights division.
* **FBI raids billionaire Stephen Cloobeck 's Beverly Hills mansion in connection with Eric Swalwell probe:** FBI agents [executed](https://substack.com/redirect/89d850f1-89ce-437d-ab1e-0af4f8b9a4ec?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a sealed search warrant on Tuesday at the Beverly Hills home of **Stephen Cloobeck** , billionaire owner of the timeshare company Diamond Resorts. **Eric Swalwell** stayed at the home several times while campaigning, an FBI spokesperson said. Swalwell dropped out of the California governor's race and resigned from Congress in April after allegations that he sexually assaulted a former staffer and acted inappropriately with other young women, which he denied.
* In August, federal agents seized Swalwell's devices, raided his Washington home, and briefly held him at San Francisco International Airport. Earlier in the summer, they searched his Dublin home. Separately, authorities in New York and Los Angeles County are investigating the ex-congressman.
* **Hackers target FEC system, disrupting campaign finance filings a week before midterms:** The Federal Elections Commission [said](https://substack.com/redirect/3d3ce1cd-c26f-4b30-985a-d36f787c43bd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Tuesday that its electronic filing system has been offline since Monday evening, forcing a shutdown of web-facing services. An FEC filings officer told compliance firms that "we have a bad actor attempting to breach FEC systems," according to an email seen by Reuters. The outage blocks 24- and 48-hour spending reports, though past reports remain searchable and voters' ability to cast ballots is unaffected.
* **Hasan Piker sues Scott Jennings for defamation over edited lynching clip:** The leftist Twitch streamer **Hasan Piker** [filed](https://substack.com/redirect/b4afd6a0-48a8-45b8-9a77-614a871f362e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a federal suit in Washington, DC, on Tuesday, alleging that the conservative commentator **Scott Jennings** aired manipulated footage of him. According to the 38-page filing, an August 11 episode of "The Scott Jennings Show" included footage of Piker that contained misleading quotations. Captions attributed to Piker the line "Let's go back to a better time when lynchings were happening." Jennings then accused him of "calling for Black voters to be lynched."
* Jennings posted the edited segment on X, and tied Piker to the Michigan Senate nominee **Abdul El-Sayed**. Jennings described Piker as El-Sayed's "best pal and campaign partner." The X post drew about 2.5 million views. Piker's suit said that Jennings refused to retract the post after receiving a written demand on August 31, and that Jennings harmed Piker's reputation and his income from streaming, advertising, and sponsorship deals.
* **Trump moves to loosen rules for oil and gas firms:** On Tuesday, President Trump [announced](https://substack.com/redirect/0794e827-2988-4a82-8180-5d6b70af4ca6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) an Environmental Protection Agency plan to weaken federal rules governing methane emissions, calling the Biden-era rules "expensive and unnecessary." The proposal would relax EPA requirements for hundreds of thousands of low-output "marginal" wells, end the agency's Methane Super Emitter Program, and reverse a rule requiring operators to capture the additional gas that leaks from wells. Although "marginal" wells make up about 7% of U.S. oil and gas production, they account for roughly half of the industry's methane emissions.
* **Supreme Court lets Texas-Justice Department deal on deportation proceedings stand:** On Tuesday, the Supreme Court [refused](https://substack.com/redirect/d10be2d6-c43c-48cf-9f28-f04c6d4c2815?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to block an agreement ending immigration judges' discretion to suspend deportation cases through "administrative closure." The procedural tool allows judges to halt deportation proceedings under certain circumstances, such as when an immigrant seeks humanitarian protection to remain in the U.S. The plaintiffs in the case, several U.S. cities and the advocacy group Centro Legal, argued in favor of the legitimacy of administrative closure.
* **NYPD cancels no-bid contract with Israeli surveillance firm:** The New York Police Department will not pursue a "sole source procurement" deal with the Israeli firm Cognyte for AI-driven surveillance technology, an NYPD spokesperson [said](https://substack.com/redirect/29975f31-51e1-46a3-ab60-9fa3ed8d8429?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Tuesday. According to the spokesperson, the firm "did not meet the criteria" for such an arrangement and that the NYPD would conduct "an open, competitive procurement process." The decision comes after allies of Mayor **Zohran Mamdani** criticized the contract. The Israeli firm's FalcoNet technology would allow police to intercept cell-phone communications. Similar technology is already used by the department, though experts say that the FalcoNet system would significantly increase police surveillance capacities.
